continues: exp2_steps_vs_quality (500/1500/5000/10000, 5 seeds) — same corpus, same split, same architecture, same loop
question: Past 10,000 steps, does the curve flatten, or does it turn back up? Every extra step re-reads a corpus the model has already seen, so the interesting failure is not 'stops helping' — it is 'starts hurting'.
why_this_is_the_right_question: At batch 32 x block 128 the model reads 4,096 characters per step.
The corpus is 19,986,068 characters, so one crossing is ~4,880 steps.
160,000 steps is ~33 crossings of the same text.
A model shown the same text 33 times can improve on text it has memorised
while getting worse at text it has not seen. That is the whole reason a
held-out set exists, and nothing in this repository has ever run long

fixed_across_every_run.split: group_split defaults (val_frac 0.1, seed 1337) — identical holdout for every run and identical to exp2
fixed_across_every_run.architecture: Medium preset: n_layer 4, n_head 4, n_embd 256, block_size 128, batch_size 32
fixed_across_every_run.lr: auto_lr(256) with the same warmup and cosine-to-lr/10 schedule train.py uses

arms.note_on_seed_count: 3 seeds, not 5. exp2 measured the seed spread at 5 seeds across four arms and found it stable and small (0.0055-0.0116). 3 seeds is the DoR's routine-comparison count; a claim-bearing rerun would use 5. This is declared here rather than discovered later.
arms.note_on_separate_runs: Each arm is its own run with its own cosine schedule, NOT a single long run sampled at checkpoints. The schedule decays to lr/10 at the declared endpoint, so a 160k run at step 20k is at a different learning rate than a 20k run at its end. Sampling one long run would compare arms that never existed.

primary_outcome: final validation loss on the fixed holdout
secondary_outcomes: generalization gap (val - train). This is the memorisation signal: a gap that widens while val stalls or rises means the model is learning the corpus rather than the language.
corpus crossings (steps * 4096 / corpus_chars), so 'how many times has it seen this text' is on the same table as the losses

success_bar.flattening: An arm counts as still improving only if its mean val loss beats the previous arm's by more than the wider of the two seed spreads — the same bar exp2 used.
success_bar.turning_up: The tail is declared FOUND if any arm's mean val loss is HIGHER than a previous arm's by more than the wider seed spread.
success_bar.memorising: Declared if the val-minus-train gap grows across arms by more than the seed spread of the gap, whether or not val itself has turned up yet.

prespecified_outcomes.if_it_turns_up: Report the step count where more training measurably made the model WORSE on unseen text, and name it as the ceiling this corpus supports at this model size.
prespecified_outcomes.if_it_only_flattens: Report that within 160,000 steps (~33 crossings) no harm was measurable, give the per-doubling gain at the far end, and say plainly that the turn-up was looked for and not found.
prespecified_outcomes.if_the_gap_widens_without_val_rising: Report memorisation as detected-but-not-yet-costly, which is the honest reading and the one the notifier would need.
prespecified_outcomes.either_way: Published. A flat tail is as useful a product fact as a rising one.

not_claimed: That these numbers transfer to another corpus, size, or vocabulary.
That validation loss says anything about whether the generated text reads well.
That 3 seeds can detect an effect smaller than the spread they measure.
That the absence of a turn-up below 160,000 steps means none exists further out.
